claims.text: Britain at war with the Ottoman Empire, early Nov 1914; Asquith, 9 Nov: the Ottoman government 'rung the death knell of Ottoman dominion'; Samuel memorandum from 21 Jan 1915; Lloyd George 'very keen to see a Jewish state'.
Kishinev, 19–21 April 1903: 47–49 killed; led Herzl to the Uganda scheme; self-defence leagues (Jabotinsky); 'tens of thousands' left for the West or Palestine.
Ottoman wartime persecution: ~7,000 Jewish refugees to Alexandria by early 1915; ~8,000 expelled from Jaffa in April 1917.
Farhud, 1–2 June 1941: 128 killed (official), 150–180 (other estimate); afterwards many young Iraqi Jews turned to Zionism; Iraqi Jews included in Zionist immigration plans in 1943.
Bevin, 18 Feb 1947: referral to the UN; the Mandate 'proved to be unworkable in practice'; no power 'to award the country'.

sources.label: Uzay Bulut, JNS (2021), on Ottoman wartime persecution of the Jews of Palestine
